subject: pathology
title: Neuropathy, myopathy and neuromuscular junction disease

steps.tx: **Guillain Barre syndrome** causes rapidly ascending weakness with absent reflexes after infections such as Campylobacter enteritis. Cerebrospinal fluid shows **albuminocytologic dissociation** because protein rises while the white cell count stays nearly normal. Autonomic instability and respiratory failure develop in severe cases, so ventilation requires close monitoring in intensive care. Treatment uses **intravenous immunoglobulin or plasmapheresis** because steroids alone do not improve recovery in this disease.
steps.say: Guillain Barre syndrome is a disorder where ascending weakness develops because peripheral nerves lose myelin after infection triggers immunity. Albuminocytologic dissociation appears because cerebrospinal fluid protein rises while cell counts remain nearly normal throughout. Steroid treatment is ineffective because controlled evidence shows no meaningful recovery benefit in this condition.

steps.tx: Vitamin B12 deficiency causes **subacute combined degeneration** because dorsal and lateral spinal cord columns lose myelin progressively. Patients lose vibration sense while developing spastic weakness because proprioceptive and corticospinal tracts fail together in the cord. Blood shows macroovalocytes with **hypersegmented neutrophils**, which links the neurological syndrome back to megaloblastic anaemia in stems. Intramuscular replacement requires urgent administration because folate alone can worsen cord damage while improving blood counts.
steps.say: Vitamin B12 deficiency damages the spinal cord because dorsal and lateral columns lose myelin over several months. Vibration loss occurs because dorsal columns carry proprioceptive signals from the legs to the brain. Urgent replacement is required because folate alone improves blood counts while cord injury keeps progressing.

steps.tx: **Duchenne muscular dystrophy** affects boys because dystrophin is absent from muscle fibres in this X linked disease. Children rise from the floor using the **Gowers sign** and show calf pseudohypertrophy despite progressive proximal weakness. Creatine kinase rises massively because fragile muscle fibres leak enzymes during repeated contraction and damage. **Dermatomyositis** differs because heliotrope eyelids and Gottron papules accompany proximal weakness and require a malignancy search.
steps.say: Duchenne dystrophy is a disease where absent dystrophin makes muscle fibres fragile during everyday childhood activity. Gowers sign appears because weak hip muscles force children to climb up their thighs when standing. Calf enlargement is misleading because fat and connective tissue replace lost muscle fibres.

vis.alt: A child demonstrating Gowers sign, using hands to stand, with an inset showing enlarged calves, characteristic of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
vis.caption: Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Gowers sign and calf pseudohypertrophy

steps.tx: **Myasthenia gravis** causes fatigable weakness because antibodies reduce acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction over time. Ptosis and diplopia worsen with activity and improve with rest, which helps separate this disease from structural nerve palsies. **Acetylcholine receptor antibodies** support diagnosis, while chest imaging searches for an associated **thymoma** in the anterior mediastinum. Pyridostigmine improves transmission symptomatically, and thymectomy benefits selected patients with generalised disease and thymic pathology.
steps.say: Myasthenia gravis is a junction disorder where antibodies reduce acetylcholine receptors and transmission becomes fatigable with activity. Ptosis improves with rest because rested junctions temporarily recover some effective transmission at the muscle endplate. Thymoma screening is essential because anterior mediastinal tumours associate strongly with this autoimmune disease.

steps.tx: This chest scan shows a lobulated **anterior mediastinal thymoma** sitting in front of the great vessels at thoracic inlet level. The inset eye photograph shows **fatigable ptosis**, which is the ocular clue that links the mass to myasthenia gravis clinically. Acetylcholine receptor antibodies and pyridostigmine appear as labels because they connect diagnosis and symptomatic treatment in one frame. Examiners use this composite because finding a thymoma changes management beyond simple drug therapy.
steps.say: This scan shows an anterior mediastinal thymoma because a lobulated mass sits in front of the great vessels. Fatigable ptosis appears in the inset because myasthenia weakens eyelid muscles after sustained upward gaze. This combination helps clinicians remember why chest imaging follows antibody testing.
